claims.text: A DFT-based method incorporating phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will improve predictive accuracy by at least 15% relative to current predictions.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in the as-cast state.
The proposed calculations are intended to apply from 300 K to 1000 K at ambient pressure.
Phonon-dispersion relations and lattice dynamics are the structural mediator used by the predictive approach.
Accurate modeling of phonon-dispersion relations and lattice dynamics enables identification of alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The method will predict phonon thermal conductivities at least 15% lower than current predictions.
The predicted reduction in phonon thermal conductivity will be at least 0.5 W m^-1 K^-1.
The comparison baseline consists of empirical models or simplified computational approaches currently used for prediction.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys containing no more than five constituent elements.
The approach is limited to alloys having a mixing entropy greater than 1.5R.
DFT accuracy and transferability to experiments may be uncertain, especially for alloys with complex chemistries or defects.
Experimental thermal conductivity will be compared with predictions for a set of alloys selected by the proposed method.
Thermal conductivity will be measured by laser flash or a similar technique.
Phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics will be measured by inelastic neutron scattering or a similar technique.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted thermal conductivity differs from experiment by more than 20%, or if predicted phonon dispersions fail to match experiment.
